### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c`.

⛔ **21** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `owner_id (literal, 46 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea04422ed25c77b30a03934a2ca900c643d06032` — the merge of head `06e7a7d36188730082a0e1b4b4a2e5a4ffb5a874` into base `5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea04422ed25c77b30a03934a2ca900c643d06032 && git checkout ea04422ed25c77b30a03934a2ca900c643d06032
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c 06e7a7d36188730082a0e1b4b4a2e5a4ffb5a874 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c && git merge --no-ff 06e7a7d36188730082a0e1b4b4a2e5a4ffb5a874

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5c5b54d3faecbac18a642c70139df295639b985c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：对象定义里新增"更改负责人"开关，可按对象打开或关闭这个操作；明细行、发票明细、系统表等本来没有真正负责人的对象，平台一律不提供。按钮和接口在后续卡里接上，现在用户界面还看不到变化。
- 为什么做：以前凡是带负责人字段的记录都可能出现"更改负责人"，管理员会在明细行等不该出现的地方看到它。
- 出错会怎样：目前没有运行时读取这个开关；在不合格对象上写"打开"会在加载定义时被拒并说明原因，不影响已有对象。
- 要你做什么：无。席位做合同复审后由区域落地。
- 席位意见：设计清楚、拒绝规则只作用于新键，证据充分，可以进入合同复审。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT, with one item before the L2** · head `5c5036bf02184202257f179ea0ff8df42177bb6c` · Fixes #35401 · 2026-11-19T16:26Z · reviewed to `pm-dispatch` text at `origin/main` `fca72dfa32`

**Readings, my own.**
- `check-governed-merges --pr 35583`: 0 of 25 paths governed.
- `merge-tree` against main: clean. K=6.
- +526/−13.
- **Claim history.** Claim 7003493133 (08:09Z, p1). Released 15:25Z at the data hand-off, as unstarted on the platform: the finished diff had been refused at commit. The release was withdrawn at 15:27Z (7013600331), on the maintainer's ask in the area thread to commit it and open a draft PR. So this is the in-flight card finished, not a new data claim.
- **Surface.** Every path is in the claimed surface: `object.zod.ts`, the eligibility helper beside `injected-system-columns.ts`, the object form rows and their generated translations, the generated baselines, the liveness ledger, reference pages, tests and `.changeset/`.

**R1 (before the L2): CI green on this head.** At this reading: 14 success, 9 skipped, 24 `in_progress`. The dev's local red, `check:platform-checklist` seed-mode-matrix VARIANTS STALE, has inputs byte-identical to `origin/main`. If CI shows it red here, show the same gate red on `main` at the merge base, so the red is main's, before queueing. Any other red needs a fix push and a fresh L1.

**Code.**
- **`transferIneligibilityReason` / `isTransferEligible`.** Eligibility is structural only: `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(def).owner`, and `owner_id` not declared `readonly`. The reason names the first structural fact, in this order: `systemFields: false`, `managedBy`, `sys_`, `business_unit`, other `ownership`, `readonly`.
- **`resolveUserActionTransfer`.** It checks eligibility first, then the authored switch (boolean, or `{ enabled, visibleWhen, disabledWhen }` with an absent `enabled` keeping the default), then `sharingModel !== 'controlled_by_parent'`. It is one function for the coming endpoint (#35402) and console action (#35403).
- **`refuseIneligibleUserActionTransfer`.** It runs in the object's `superRefine` and refuses only an opening value (`true` / `{ enabled: true }`), at `userActions.transfer`, with the reason. Closing, or a predicate-only form, is accepted.
- **Aliases.** `userActions` was already a `strictObject` on main (line 3731), so `changeOwner` / `reassign` were already refused as unknown keys. The added aliases only point them at `transfer`.

**Declaration: agreed.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added` / `Skills-docs: none` with its reason: no skill teaches object-level `userActions`; the five hits are the view and page block.
- The refusal arrives with the key it guards (the d635555 precedent). No stored object can carry `transfer`, so no accepted input is newly refused, and no narrowing arm is owed.
- The liveness ledger records the child as PLANNED under ruling 7000907189 point 1. The parse refusal is live, and the reading turns live with #35402 and #35403, both Blocked-by this card.

**Changeset sentences checked against the diff:**
- "derived, never overridable", plus the ownership, managedBy, sys_, systemFields and readonly list;
- the switch shape and the sharingModel default, both ways;
- "the one resolution";
- refused at parse, closing accepted, the `changeOwner` / `reassign` pointers;
- "gates the dedicated action, not the raw write";
- the Studio form row and its translations;
- "nothing reads the switch at runtime yet".

**Pins (names grepped).** `user-action-transfer.test.ts` covers:
- eligibility: user or omitted ownership; never `sys_`; never under `systemFields: false`; readonly vs writable `owner_id`; parsed equals bare; non-object input;
- resolution: omitted sharingModel; a `controlled_by_parent` opt-in; a private opt-out; predicates and a predicate-only form; ineligible stays off; parsed schema;
- parse: accepts both ways on eligible; accepts `true` on a parent-controlled detail; refuses on `sys_` and on readonly `owner_id`; accepts closing on ineligible; refuses `changeOwner` with the pointer.

**Overlap.** One count pin (`object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`) is shared with draft #35510. Whichever lands second merges main and sets 745. No queueing order is needed.

**Routing.** L2 is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (published `packages/spec/src/**`) by seat 5, on the green head. It is not governed, so data-2 lands it after the L2.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5c5036bf02184202257f179ea0ff8df42177bb6c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts + packages/spec/liveness/object.json

Read: card #35401 with its four comments (claim 7003493133, release 7013535406, withdrawal 7013600331, dev report 7015117249), PR #35583 body, its 25 files and the net diff against `main` (merge base `cf6bb70e2d`; `main` has moved 11 commits since, none on a path this PR touches), rulings 7000556646 and 7000907189 on #35315, sibling cards #35402 and #35403, and the check-runs on the head: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, widened: right.** `ObjectSchema.userActions.transfer` is newly accepted as `boolean | RowCrudActionOverrideSchema`, the union its four CRUD siblings take. `userActions` was already a strict block on `main`, so `transfer` was an unknown-key refusal before.
- **The new refusal narrows nothing: right.** `refuseIneligibleUserActionTransfer` reads only the new key, so no input `main` accepts is refused here. `changeOwner` and `reassign` were unknown-key refusals on `main` and stay refusals, now with a pointer. No narrowing arm, no ADR-0087 entry and no migration are owed: no stored object can carry the key.
- **Public surface, added only: right.** Four exports reach `@objectstack/spec/data` through `export *` (`isTransferEligible`, `transferIneligibilityReason`, `resolveUserActionTransfer`, `UserActionTransferResolution`); `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly those four.
- **Reference pages: right.** `object.mdx` gains the `transfer` row and the container sentence changes on the three pages that print it. The hand-written guide `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` (line 330) still lists five keys; staying silent there is correct while nothing offers the action, and the row is owed by #35403.
- **Form and translations: right in count.** One composite row, two leaves, in all eleven bundles; the pins move 115 to 117, 104 to 106 and 741 to 742, which is what one label plus one help text gives. For the lane, outside ④: the composite's own `userActions` help text gained a sentence in `en` only; the ten translated bundles keep the old value.
- **Permission surface: unchanged at this head.** The diff touches no file under `plugin-security`, `plugin-sharing`, `objectql` or `rest`. Nothing outside the parse reads the key or calls the three helpers (grep at the head: `object.zod.ts` and the test file only), so the declaration can neither grant nor withhold a transfer; a plain `owner_id` write is governed exactly as on `main`.
- **Liveness verdict: wrong.** The ledger's machine reading for `object.userActions.transfer` at this head is `live`, inherited from the container's blanket row, while the PR's own note says PLANNED. See M1.
- **Structural eligibility: wrong for one object class.** See S1.
- **Gates.** `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core`, `Type Check UI` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all concluded success on the head. The liveness gate is green because a recorded undrilled container asks nothing of its children; that is the gap M1 names, not an answer to it.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/35401-user-actions-transfer.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` minor. Correct: the kind is `added`, both packages are moved by the diff, and a kind takes at least minor on each.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agreed, on the PR body and in the changeset body, line-initial in both. A new authorable key and four new exports; no accepted input is refused, so no `(narrowing)` arm and no BREAKING banner.

Metadata-protocol: added — agreed, in both places. A new key only; `narrowed` and `semantic` do not apply.

For the lane (changesets are outside ④): bullet 3 says the endpoint and the console action "both read it", and the closing paragraph says nothing reads the switch yet. The closing paragraph is the true one at this head, and the text ships as CHANGELOG.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **A1** (reuse `RowCrudActionOverrideSchema`; not added to the write-locked buckets) — right. `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` withholds the owner column for every truthy `managedBy`, so the structural test already refuses `transfer: true` on each bucket; the test pins all seven.
- **A2** (the container stays recorded as undrilled, the planned verdict lives in the note) — wrong. M1.
- **A3** (`sharingModel` omitted resolves the default to on) — right. The `sharingModel` describe on `main` states that a custom object omitting it resolves to `private` (ADR-0090 D1), and `controlled_by_parent` is only ever declared, never derived.
- **open_questions 1** (four-line maintainer brief against the six-line form) — not a contract question; `PR-body guards` concluded success. Nothing to rule at this tier.
- **open_questions 2** (count pin shared with draft PR #35510) — option A is safe, no queue order is needed. Both PRs rewrite the same line (`toBe(741)` in `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`), so the second cannot merge textually clean and must merge `main`; the pin is an exact equality inside `Test Core`, so a wrong resolution reds the queue build and cannot land. 741 + 1 here + 3 there = 745. Read in #35510's patches: its other pins (12 to 14 in the hook panels) are in files this PR does not touch, and it does not touch this PR's 115/117 and 104/106 pins.
- **out_of_scope finding** (`check:platform-checklist` red in the dev's container) — `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success on this head, so the red is not this diff's. The lane's.
- **deviations** (`commit-tree` re-record of unpublished commits; worktree kept) — no contract effect.
- **Skills-docs: none** — agreed. The `userActions` hits under `skills/` are `objectstack-ui` list-view and navigation rules and their evals, the view block.
- **Not flagged by the dev, for #35402:** `UserActionTransferResolution.predicates` documents what the two predicates do to the button. Neither the ruling nor card #35402 says how the endpoint reads them. That card should state it before it consumes the helper; no finding on this head.
- **SQL push-down:** no query path in the diff; nothing to judge.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/liveness/object.json` (implementing) and the declaration it grades**

M1 (must-fix) — `userActions.transfer` ships declared, unread and unmarked. At this head the accepted values of the key change no runtime behaviour: `transfer: false`, `transfer: true` on a detail, and both predicates are read by nothing (the parse reads the key only to refuse one value on ineligible objects). Shipping a key ahead of its reader is allowed, in the marked form: ADR-0049's second state, which the ledger spells as a `planned` row. More than thirty rows carry it today, `enable.aiReadable` in this same file among them, and the README records the form for exactly this shape under `page.print`: "its REFUSALS live ... its keys `planned` with `authorWarn` on the container". This PR instead writes PLANNED in the `note` of a row whose `status` is `live`. The consequences are all mechanical:
  - the gate and `lint-liveness-properties` read `live` for the child, so no author is told the switch does nothing yet, and the README defines `live` as "authoring the property changes runtime behaviour";
  - a `note` is, in the README's words, never shown to an author, and the two `file#symbol` anchors in it are not resolved by the gate, which checks `evidence` and `producer` only;
  - `undrilled-containers.baseline.json` describes `object/userActions` as a container whose child keys are "classified NOWHERE", and names "a reassuring sentence in a `note`" as the thing the baseline replaced. The README's rule for this case is "Drill where the audit gives divergent sub-statuses", and this PR creates the divergence.
  The L1 note on this PR reads the ledger as recording the child PLANNED, which is the misreading the prose invites. Fix: drill `object/userActions` (a `children` map; the five existing keys with their readers' evidence, `resolveCrudAffordances` and its callers being where to start; `transfer` as `planned` with `authorWarn: true`, an `authorHint`, and the refusal and resolver anchors moved into `evidence`), and remove the coordinate from the undrilled baseline. With the row warning at `os lint` and `os validate`, the describe and the Studio help text can stay written for the shipped state.

**`packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`**

S1 (should-fix) — the structural test reads less than the spec readers it stands beside, in two places.
  - An ADR-0015 `external` object that neither declares `owner_id` nor maps a remote column onto it answers `isTransferEligible: true`, and `resolveUserActionTransfer` answers on by default. `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(def).owner` is true there, but the column is registered and stored nowhere: `injected-system-column-provenance.ts` grades it `injected-unprovisioned`, and `isOwnerAnchorUnprovable` is the reader plugin-sharing and lint already use for "no owner is provable". So the parse accepts `transfer: true` on an object with no owner to change, the "switch nothing honours" the refusal exists to stop, and the helper's sentence "whose records have a reassignable owner" is false for it. The ruling names two clauses and its "so" list does not mention external objects. Either add the arm, with its reason clause and a pin, or put the maintainer's word that such objects stay eligible on the card.
  - `ownerFieldDeclaredReadonly` reads the record shape of `fields` only. `readDeclaredFieldDef` in the sibling module reads both registered shapes, record and array, and the docblock here claims the same tolerance as `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`. On an array-shaped document a pinned owner reads as eligible. Read both shapes, or narrow the docblock's claim.

The rest of the file holds. The reason clauses follow the resolver's own order. A non-object input fails closed. The resolution checks eligibility before the switch, so a document that skipped the parse still answers off. The predicate-only form keeps the derived default, as `normalizeRowCrudOverride` does for the CRUD entries.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`**

The refusal sits in the existing callback beside `refuseWriteLockedUserActions`, adds no check node, locates one issue at `userActions.transfer`, and names the structural reason. The union and the two alias pointers are as the ruling asks.

S2 (should-fix) — one sibling of the key was not moved with it. `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls-references.ts` classifies the `userActions` block key by key: `create`, `import`, `edit` and `delete` as `crudFlag`, `exportCsv` as `keep`. `transfer` is the same union and is unlisted, so it takes the unclassified path and the served document treats it differently from its four siblings. That file's header says a new spec key is classified on the day it lands. Add `transfer: crudFlag` with its pin, here or on a card that blocks #35403, the first reader of the served switch.

N1 (nit) — the refusal's prescription does not fit every arm. "Remove the entry, or make the object owner-bearing" is wrong for the readonly arm, where the object is owner-bearing and the way out is to drop `readonly`. "may only narrow" (here and in the `isTransferEligible` docblock) reads against `transfer: true` opening a `controlled_by_parent` detail.

N2 (nit) — prose beside the key was not carried. The guidance strings in the same block still say the object block "governs CRUD affordances (create/import/edit/delete/exportCsv)" and "CRUD affordances only", and the `userActions` JSDoc still describes only the `managedBy`-derived default.

N3 (nit) — a predicate-only `transfer` on an ineligible object is accepted and inert. The ruling names `enabled: true` only, so this follows it; an accepted deviation.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts`**

Holds. The row takes the `json` face its four union siblings take, the comment counts six keys, and the composite's help text says the entry is outside the `managedBy` matrix. The row is offered on every object, and an ineligible object refuses it loudly at save.

**`packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`**

Holds. One `export *` beside `injected-system-columns`. N4 (nit) — the comment, like the module docblock, says the endpoint and the console action "both read" the resolution; at this head neither exists.
